newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts close little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts close little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ short end rallies a touch on strong currency
* Bonds fail to test lower as profit-takers step in
* Yields still seen lower in medium term
New Zealand debt markets closed largely unchanged on Wednesday in quiet trade despite the currency briefly touching an 8-1/2 year high.
Dealers said the Kiwi dollar's strength had sparked bidding interest in the short end, where the 90-day bank bill yield fell three points to 8.91 percent, but bond yields failed to follow suit.

"The surprising thing is the bill futures have been running around a little bit, but the bonds have been very quiet. They haven't been sucked into any sort of rally on the back of the strength in the currency at all," one dealer said.
He said profit-taking had put an end to a rally prompted by weaker-than-expected wages data on Tuesday.
"This has been the bottom end of the recent ranges we've been trading in in the last few weeks so people are just taking a bit of profit," he said.
Dealers said the expectation was for yields to move lower in the medium term, but in the short term the market could struggle to break out of its range.

"There seems to be just a little bit of stock around at the moment -- until we clean that out we might just struggle to get through seven percent in those mid stocks," a dealer said. ---------------------------------------------------------------- Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
